judgment.explanation: The proposed message asks the customer (Melli Orven) to upload the warehouse receipt, but the evidence already shows the receipt exists. In event-001, the warehouse sent inline receipt WH-035 to Iona Quill / Rivet Delivery Desk, confirming RT-035 for TG-035 was received at 08:10 UTC. In event-002, the customer asked the desk to pass the receipt to the team that handles refund review. The blocker is therefore internal: the desk should forward the receipt to the refund-review team, or confirm who owns that step. It should not ask the customer for evidence the desk already holds. The recipient is wrong because the customer is not the party who needs to act. The message also implies the customer must supply the document before review can start, which is not supported by the visible evidence and sends the customer back around a loop she is trying to escape. It does not name the refund-review team, which is not identified in the visible events and would need internal confirmation. It does not acknowledge her request or give a status update. The wording is clear and polite, but it is the wrong request. Nothing is fabricated as completed, though the claim that an upload is required is an unsupported policy. As an unsent proposal it makes no unauthorized commitment, but it does not address who is authorized to approve a refund review.
